{{Quote|The Finbat is one of the best ways of taking out an AT-AT ever invented.|"[[Jorsk]]," in an annotation to ''[[Gundark's Gear Datalog]]''|<ref name="Gundark's" />}}
The [[Kessler/Legends|Kessler]] '''J8Q-128 Finbat Missile''' was a portable [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] designed to be shoulder-fired by a lone individual. It was created to eliminate large, heavily-[[Armor/Legends|armored]] targets such as [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Walker/Legends|walkers]]. While effective in its role, the missile itself moved slowly, and a capable [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] could shoot down the missile mid-flight. Introduced prior to the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the weapon was snapped up quickly by the [[Black market/Legends|black market]], and was still in production within the borders of the [[Pentastar Alignment]] after the fragmentation of the Empire.

==Description==
{{Quote|I bet the Imperials were shocked the day a lone Rebel waltzed over, set up the launcher and fired a missile into the neck of the nearest walker.|"[[Mal'urc]]," in an annotation to ''[[Gundark's Gear Datalog]]''|<ref name="Gundark's" />}}
The J8Q-128 Finbat Missile was a portable, shoulder-fired, anti-[[Walker/Legends|walker]] [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] developed by [[Kessler/Legends|Kessler]]. It was designed for use by a single person, from preparation to firing; after firing, the launch tube was discarded. Designed to destroy large, slow-moving targets such as [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-ATs]] and [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-STs]], the missile itself moved slowly, and could potentially be shot down by a competent [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] mid-flight.<ref name="Blasters for Hire" /> The warhead was specifically designed to overcome the heavy plating of an AT-AT,<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|129|J8Q-128 Finbat}}</ref> and consisted of four separate segments to penetrate the [[Armor/Legends|armor]] of its targets; the final explosive within the body of the missile was designed to fragment and continue moving through the target, inflicting significant internal damage.<ref name="Blasters for Hire" /> Even a first-time Finbat user could decapitate an AT-AT with the weapon.<ref name="Gundark's" /> However, the missile was limited to a range of approximately 500 [[Meter/Legends|meters]], and was less effective when not delivered against a foe squarely in the weapon's sights, tending to bounce off the side of the target. The missile sold for four thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="Blasters for Hire" />

==History==
{{Quote|Leave it to Kessler to build something to swat a walker, right under the noses of the Alignment and the rest of the Empire.|[[Sully Tigereye]]|<ref name="Blasters for Hire" />}}
Kessler developed the Finbat Missile prior to the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. When first introduced to the [[Black market/Legends|black market]], the units were purchased so quickly that the Empire did not notice them. Several months before the Battle of Hoth, the [[Arms dealer/Legends|arms dealer]] [[Gundark (arms dealer)|Gundark]] acquired samples of the missiles and made them available through ''[[Gundark's Gear Datalog]]'', his inventory [[Scandoc/Legends|scandoc]].<ref name="Gundark date">The first comment on the ''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]'' entry for the Finbat is dated 38:2:1, predating the 38:6:6 date given in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' for the events depicted in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']].</ref> The missiles were used by both [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] forces and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] against Imperial walkers.<ref name="Gundark's" /> Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], numerous warlord fiefdoms broke away from the Empire, among them [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Ardus Kaine]]'s [[Pentastar Alignment]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Kessler continued to produce the Finbat within the Pentastar Alignment's jurisdiction, without the knowledge of the Alignment or other parts of the Empire. Finbat Missiles were among the weapons familiar to the [[Red Moons]], a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] organization hostile to the Alignment.<ref name="Blasters for Hire" />

==Behind the scenes==
The J8Q-128 Finbat Missile first appeared in "[[Blasters for Hire]]: A Mercenary's Guidebook," an in-universe [[New Republic era|New Republic]] article written by [[Tony Russo|Anthony P. Russo]] for [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 3|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 3]], released in [[1994]]. In [[1997]], it was featured again in ''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]'', a compilation of personal equipment that had appeared in previous ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' materials. It was not mentioned again until the [[2008]] publication of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.
